{{Field procedure|summary=Process mined commodity fragments into whole tonnes while keeping refinery bins and cargo capacity available.}}

A ship [[Refinery|refinery]] separates the commodity components in collected asteroid fragments. Each component accumulates in a bin assigned to that commodity. At 100%, the refinery creates one tonne and transfers it to free cargo capacity.<ref name="refinery">[https://elite-dangerous.fandom.com/wiki/Refinery Refinery], ''Elite Dangerous Wiki''. Accessed 16 September 2026.</ref>

This procedure covers normal operation during a mining run. Module classes, ratings, bin counts and Engineering belong to [[Refinery]]. Use [[How to Resolve a Full Refinery]] when processing has already stopped.

== Before you start ==

* Fit and power one refinery. A larger bin count allows more partial commodities to be held at the same time; it does not make individual fragments process faster.
* Fit at least one [[Cargo Rack]] and leave capacity for completed tonnes. Limpets also occupy cargo space until launched.
* Carry a collection method. [[Collector Limpet Controller|Collector limpets]] are the normal choice for repeated mining fragments, although fragments can also be scooped manually.
* Decide which commodities the run should keep before extraction begins.

Raw Engineering materials do not enter the refinery. They transfer to dedicated material storage and do not consume a bin or cargo-rack space.

== Procedure ==

{{Procedure steps|
# Confirm the refinery and cargo hatch are powered and that the cargo hold has room for at least one completed tonne.
# Extract the wanted resource with the mining method appropriate to the deposit.
# Open the cargo scoop and retrieve the released fragments. If using autonomous collectors, launch them without targeting a collectable object.
# Open the refinery display in the ship's right-hand panel and watch the incoming components enter matching or empty bins.
# Let later fragments add progress to each matching bin. A mixed fragment can advance more than one commodity bin.
# When a bin reaches 100%, confirm that one tonne appears in cargo and any progress beyond 100% remains toward the next tonne.<ref name="refinery" />
# Continue collecting while monitoring bin occupancy, cargo capacity and unwanted resources.
# Before leaving the site, allow collectors to deliver the remaining wanted fragments and confirm that no useful incoming resource is blocked.
}}

Processing is automatic when a matching or empty bin and a valid destination are available. The percentage shown in a bin is progress toward one tonne, not an amount that can be sold before completion.

== Managing bins ==

Each bin holds only one commodity at a time. Partially filled bins remain assigned until their commodity completes or the bin is vented. A run targeting many resources therefore needs more bins than a single-commodity run.<ref name="refinery" />

* Use [[How to Ignore Unwanted Mining Commodities]] before collectors retrieve low-priority fragments. Ignoring future contacts does not clear a bin already in use.
* Vent a partial bin only after confirming that its progress is not wanted. Venting destroys that accumulated material.
* If all bins are occupied and an incoming fragment contains a different commodity, either free a low-priority bin, discard the obstructing incoming resource or stop collecting that resource.
* If a mixed fragment contains both wanted and unwanted components, keep enough bin capacity for the wanted component before allowing collection to continue.

== Cargo interaction ==

A completed tonne must move into a cargo rack before its bin can resume normal use. If the cargo hold is full, a 100% bin remains occupied until at least one tonne of cargo capacity becomes available.<ref name="refinery" />

Consumed limpets normally create cargo space during a run. Do not assume that this will always keep pace with refining, especially when few collectors are used or fragments contain high concentrations.

== Completion check ==

The refinery path is healthy when:

* wanted fragments increase the expected bin percentages;
* each completed bin transfers a tonne into cargo;
* incoming fragments are not waiting for a matching or empty bin; and
* collectors can deliver without holding fragments beneath the cargo hatch.

== Common problems ==

* '''A completed bin remains at 100%:''' the cargo hold has no free one-tonne slot, or the refinery is not powered. Free cargo capacity and recheck the module state.
* '''All bins are occupied:''' vent the least useful partial bin only if losing that progress is acceptable, or stop collecting the new resource.
* '''Collectors wait beneath the ship:''' confirm the scoop and cargo hatch state, then inspect cargo capacity, refinery bins and the incoming resource. Continue with [[How to Resolve a Full Refinery]].
* '''Unwanted bins keep returning:''' add the named resource to the contact ignore list with [[How to Ignore Unwanted Mining Commodities]].
* '''A raw material does not appear in a bin:''' this is normal. Engineering materials bypass the refinery and enter material storage.
* '''Collected canisters bypass the refinery:''' ordinary cargo canisters already contain whole cargo and go directly to cargo racks when eligible.
* '''The refinery shows no progress:''' verify that the collected object is a mined commodity fragment, the module is powered and a matching or empty bin is available.
